newsitem.title: CANADA: New Inmet chief pledges improvements.
newsitem.headline: New Inmet chief pledges improvements.

text.p: The new president and chief executive of Inmet Mining Corp said on Wednesday he aims to make the troubled gold and metals miner "hum."
"I'll do my best for them, try to make it hum a little bit. Have a little fun, do a few deals," Bill James said in a telephone interview after his appointment to Inmet was announced earlier today.
James, 67, a veteran mining executive, starts work for Inmet today, but will also remain as president of Denison Mines Ltd until he can be replaced.
Inmet has had a poor year so far.
The company has been hurt by low ore grades, poor copper prices and writedowns. It lost C$0.19 a share in the second quarter.

James said he wanted to turn around the company's fortunes. "They've got some mines that are problems. We'll have to do something about that," he said. "The company hasn't been performing. They had a bit of a run of tough luck, so we'll try to pepper it up a little bit."
James has had lots of practice turning companies around, said Alf Powis, a Noranda Inc board member and former Noranda chief executive.
"He went in and rescued Falconbridge in the 80s and then went in to rescue Denison," said Powis, who worked with James at Noranda in the 1970s.
James became president and chief executive of Falconbridge Ltd in 1982 and moved to Denison in 1990.
"He's a really good mining man," Powis said.
James replaces Klaus Zeitler at Inmet. Company officials would not say why they made the change.
One of James's first jobs will be to examine a strategic review of Inmet and make recommendations to the board.
A special board committee and financial advisers assembled reports, which are ready for presentation to James, the company said.
The review was started early this year because of investor concern the company lacked focus.
Focus was one of James's top priorities, he said.
"One of the things you learn is that when things look almost impossible, you keep working away at it and things tend to work out," he said.
